To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the photo-cataloging activities of phytohromones on semiconductor nanoparticles are highly dependent on laser influx, electric field strength, and the kinetic energy of photoelectrons.

the photo-cata-lytic activities of plant hormones on semiconductor nanoparticles by laser-activated electron tunneling and emitting are highly dependent on both kinetic energy of tunnel electrons and strength of laser influx.
photo-chemical reactions of organic adsorbates on semiconductor nanoparticle surfaces can be induced by ultrafast electron tunnelings.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the dynamic process of electron tunneling from the conduction band to the valence band of semiconductor nanoparticles, and the effect of laser-induced tunneling on the photo-catalysis of organic molecules adsorbed onto the surface of semiconductor nanoparticles.
the fundamental understanding and applications of the photo-catalysis mechanism of plant hormones on semiconductor surfaces.
the fundamental processes of laser-activated electron tunneling and its application in photo-chemistry and photo-catalysis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the photo catalytic activity of semiconductor nanoparticles is highly dependent on laser-induced ultrafast tunneling of electrons.

the photo-cata-lytic activities of adsorbents in the presence of laser-induced ultra-fast electron tunneling are determined by the kinetic energy of photoelectrons and the number of electron tunneling events.
laser-excited electrons can be used to initiate chemical reactions in the presence of a static electric field.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the photo-activity of a given molecule is determined by the kinetic energy of photoelectrons as well as the intrinsic mobility of semiconductive nanoparticles.
the photo catalytic activity of semiconductor nanoparticles is determined by the intrinsic electron mobility of the semiconductor, and the strength of laser-induced electron tunneling.
the photo-cata-lytic activity of adsorbed molecules on semiconductors is determined by the number of resultant photoelectrons and their kinetic energies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the photo-cleavage of organic molecules is highly dependent on laser intensity, electric field, and the intrinsic properties of semiconducting materials.
laser-activated electron tunneling and emitting are the key processes for the photo-chemical and photo-catalytic reactions of semiconductor nanoparticles.
photo-catalytic reactions are highly dependent on laser pulse intensity.
